html:
Remark. Proton-mass substrate identity — numerical verification, h-expansion, and precision frontier

This note collects the numerical verification, the per-order h-expansion, the combined nucleon-mass derivation, and the sub-ppm precision frontier for prop:proton-mass-substrate-identity.

The predictive content throughout is the dimensionless ratio m_p/m_e (equivalently 2(m_\mu/m_e)F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 12): since m_e (CAL-1) sets the MeV scale by fiat, the absolute proton mass in MeV is not an independent framework prediction. The MeV figures below are that ratio rendered against the m_e unit — a rendering that lets the ratio be read off against CODATA, not an absolute-mass claim.

Per-order h-expansion in MeV

At h_0 = q_0 - q_0^{-1} \approx 0.2091, using the exact rational h-expansion of F_{\mathrm{Bor}} (categorical, def:f-bor-borromean-observable) the per-order MeV contributions to m_p = 2 m_\mu F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - 12 m_e are:

Order Coefficient 2 m_\mu \cdot c_k \cdot h_0^k
h^0 6 +1267.9\,\mathrm{MeV}
h^1 -9 -397.6\,\mathrm{MeV}
h^2 19/2 +87.7\,\mathrm{MeV}
h^3 -57/8 -13.8\,\mathrm{MeV}
-12 m_e — -6.1\,\mathrm{MeV}
Sum \approx 938.1\,\mathrm{MeV}

The series converges to 0.017\,\mathrm{ppm} accuracy at order h^9.

Combined with the canonical flavor-split

prop:flavor-split-substrate gives the canonical Hecke-skein derivation

  \frac{m_n - m_p}{M_N} \;=\; \frac{(q-1)^2(1 - q^{-4})}{3}
  \;=\; \frac{\hbar_q^2 \cdot h \cdot [2]_q}{3}

(matching CODATA \Delta m / M_N to -0.10\%, NOT a fit — each factor has explicit categorical meaning).

Combining the proposition with the flavor-split derives both nucleon masses from only (m_e, m_\mu, q_0):

  • m_p = 2 \cdot m_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q_0) - 12 \cdot m_e \approx 938.27186\,\mathrm{MeV} (0.24\,\mathrm{ppm} residual)
  • m_n = m_p + \mathfrak{Q}_\beta + m_e, with \mathfrak{Q}_\beta the parameter-free Kashiwara b^2 truncation (near-match) \approx 939.56542\,\mathrm{MeV} (\sim +1\,\mathrm{ppb} residual)
  • \mathfrak{Q}_\beta := m_n - m_p - m_e is DERIVED, not an input (+1.25\,\mathrm{ppm} on \mathfrak{Q}_\beta itself; \sim 1\,\mathrm{ppb} once propagated to m_n). The flavor-split m_n = m_p(1 + X/(1-X/2)) (below) is a secondary diagnostic ratio (-1.76\,\mathrm{ppm} on m_n), not the production route.

The flavor-split X is an h^3-leading quantity:

  X = \tfrac{1}{6}h^3 - \tfrac{1}{12}h^4 + \tfrac{1}{32}h^5 - \cdots

with h^0 = h^1 = h^2 = 0. The neutron-proton mass difference \Delta_{pn} = m_p \cdot X/(1 - X/2) is therefore a cubic effect in the deformation parameter h, not a quadratic one. The dominant MeV contributions are h^3: +1.43\,\mathrm{MeV}, h^4: -0.15\,\mathrm{MeV}.

The secondary flavor-split diagnostic's m_n residual (2.0 ppm) separates: 0.24\,\mathrm{ppm} from F_{\mathrm{Bor}} (proton mass) and 1.76\,\mathrm{ppm} from X (the flavor-split formula). Routing the neutron through the categorical \mathfrak{Q}_\beta (Kashiwara b^2) instead removes the X term: the production m_n residual drops to \sim 1\,\mathrm{ppb} and the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta residual to +1.25\,\mathrm{ppm} (on \mathfrak{Q}_\beta itself).

The 3-calibration discipline reduces to 2 calibrations (m_e, m_\mu/m_e) for the baryon and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta sector. This equates to (m_e, q_0) via the muon-anchor identity m_\mu/m_e = \mathrm{Vol}(4_1)/\hbar_q^2.

Consistency gap: decay-rate cross-check

The production neutron directly consumes the parameter-free Kashiwara b^2 categorical \mathfrak{Q}_\beta \approx 0.78233\,\mathrm{MeV}, so the flavor-split mass-derived \mathfrak{Q}_\beta and the categorical ladder agree at the production level.

A decay-width cross-check connects both derivations to experimental lifetimes via the Fermi theory: \mathfrak{D}_\mu = G_F^2 \mathfrak{m}_\mu^5 / (192\pi^3) and \mathfrak{D}_n \propto G_F^2 \mathfrak{Q}_\beta^5 f(\mathfrak{Q}_\beta/\mathfrak{m}_e), where \mathfrak{D}_K = \hbar / (\text{lifetime of } K) is the decay width in the paper's fraktur-observable convention (avoiding collision with \tau = fibre functor and \Gamma = sheaf sections). The ratio \mathfrak{D}_\mu / \mathfrak{D}_n eliminates G_F and provides a \mathfrak{Q}_\beta-independent consistency test. If both \mathfrak{m}_\mu and \mathfrak{Q}_\beta are substrate-derived, the lifetime ratio \hbar/\mathfrak{D}_n \div \hbar/\mathfrak{D}_\mu matches CODATA (\approx 4 \times 10^8) strictly from categorical invariants.

Open work for full categorical proof

The categorical structure of F_{\mathrm{Bor}} + its rational h-expansion are completed in def:f-bor-borromean-observable. What remains specific to this archimedean evaluation:

  1. Bridge from \dim V_{(2,1)} to linear factor in mass formula. The factored form m_p = \dim V_{(2,1)} \cdot (m_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}} - |S_3| \cdot m_e) is numerically exact at 50 dps but the categorical WHY — why the trace-dominant irrep's dimension enters linearly — remains a formal gap. The Wedderburn block expansion of the Markov trace provides the natural framework (the (2,1) block carries 49% of the proton's T_1 contribution), but the formal categorical statement is pending.

Sub-ppm precision frontier

The identity matches CODATA at -0.24\,\mathrm{ppm}. A near-match candidate for closing the residual to \sim 0.054\,\mathrm{ppm} is

  \mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{p}
  \;=\;
  \dim V_{(2,1)} \cdot \bigl(\mathfrak{m}_\mu \cdot F_{\mathrm{Bor}}(q_0)
  \;-\;
  \lvert S_3 \rvert \cdot \mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{e}\bigr)
  \;+\;
  \frac{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}{\pi \cdot \dim H_3} \cdot \mathfrak{m}_\mathfrak{e}.

The correction (\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}/\pi) / \dim H_3 = (\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}/\pi) / 6 appeared at 0.054 ppm (vs the bare identity's 32 ppm residual to integer 12) — a 600\times improvement, computed by ocneanu-12-em-correction-candidate. Both factors are structurally motivated: (\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}/\pi) appears in m_K/m_π's Bring zero-mode closure, and 1/\dim H_3 is the Plancherel-mean normalization over the H_3 Wedderburn block.

A Bring zero-mode template transfer and an enumeration of 27 alternative knot-operator geometries both confirmed that 1/\dim H_3 = 1/6 is the structurally robust denominator, but no transfer of the m_K/m_π (3q^2-1)/(2q^2) shape gives a tighter form. The 54 ppb residual after the EM correction is either (a) a non-trivial categorical f(q) factor with f(q_0) \approx 1.00167 not yet identified, or (b) higher-order QED / categorical corrections at the substrate precision floor. This correction remains a near-match candidate, not an established categorical derivation.

The Ocneanu-weight cancellation behind the -12\,m_e term carries a universal leading-pole coefficient -1/12. That coefficient rests on high-precision numerical pole detection, verified to 200 decimal places; the symbolic Hoefsmit route to the cancellation count still carries unrepaired convention and sign issues, so the coefficient is numerically verified rather than symbolically derived.
